common_name: Northern Lights Lungwort (Frosted Silver Multicolor-Flowered Pulmonaria)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early spring or early fall in consistently moist, humus-rich soil with good air movement to limit powdery mildew.

directions: Northern Lights carries heavily frosted, silvered foliage that sets off shimmering flowers opening in rich shades of cranberry, purple, and blue all on the same plant as the blooms age and shift color. Flower production is unusually heavy, with an extended spring bloom period and notably better mildew resistance than many older lungwort selections. The clump forms a dense, mounded patch under deciduous shade, useful as a groundcover beneath trees and shrubs. Keep soil evenly moist with good air circulation around the foliage, since humid, stagnant conditions can still bring on leaf spot in a wet season.

common_name: Permafrost Siberian Bugloss (Silvery Dark-Veined Blue-Flowered Brunnera)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Permafrost, patented under the cultivar name 'Balbrupost' and marketed through Darwin Perennials (Ball Horticultural Company's perennial division), carries silvery foliage traced with dark green veins and margins, giving a frosted, high-contrast look through the shade garden season. Medium blue flowers with a small white eye open in a cloud above the foliage in spring, in the same forget-me-not style as the species but on a moderately vigorous, mounded plant. Grow in partial to full shade in consistently moist, humus-rich soil; brunnera foliage can scorch if the soil dries out in full sun. Divide congested clumps in spring or fall to maintain vigor and foliage quality.
sources: Darwin Perennials / Ball Horticultural plant protection records

common_name: Frostline Siberian Bugloss (Yellow-Margined Silver Blue-Flowered Brunnera)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Frostline, patented under the cultivar name 'Balbrufline' and marketed through Darwin Perennials (Ball Horticultural Company's perennial division), pairs silvery leaf centers with dark green venation and a bright yellow-green margin, a variegated take on the classic silver-leaved brunnera look. Small medium-blue flowers with a white eye rise above the foliage in a loose spray in spring, echoing forget-me-nots. The bright leaf margin adds a warmer accent to shaded plantings that might otherwise rely only on cool silver and green tones. Grow in partial to full shade in evenly moist, humus-rich soil, dividing clumps every few years as they become crowded.
sources: Darwin Perennials / Ball Horticultural plant protection records
